examples.knowledge_point: Identifying the Intervals on Which a Function is Invertible Given Its Graph
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/d965e0b1087ad45206dd9259c963609f556bf5803af47ab18006bf40dffb2557.png)

     

On which of the following intervals is the function $f(x)$ (shown above) invertible?

- $(-3,-1]$

- $(0,4]$

- $[-2,2)$
examples.worked_solution:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.   

- The given function is invertible on the interval $x\in (-3,-1].$  Indeed, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/245484a6a77160a5f5892738a7e1f8e488f6df8e4ba990bbc94ae964c3305525.png)

- The given function is **not** invertible on the intervals $(0,4]$ and $[-2,2)$ because some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/4737a1460e1abd4edc200404407fef10761f038d9a29e52ba0f8c3e8c69bb93f.png)

          

Therefore, the correct answer is "I  only".

Which of the graphs above correspond to an invertible function?
feedback.worked_solution:
A function is invertible if and only if it's a one-to-one function. To determine which of the functions are one-to-one, we use the horizontal line test.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/2a68cbeceea9173ab7a53d334d073e9779b048ad8946fd3ff81b09adb79cee98.png)

From the above, we see that:

- For graph II, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line. Therefore, graph II shows a one-to-one function. As a result, this function is invertible.

- For graphs I, III and IV, some horizontal lines intersect the curve more than once. These are not one-to-one functions. As a result, they are not invertible.
